ns2:section.sectionText: In the first part of this seminar, we will explore the history of the concept of voluntariness in Western philosophy, focusing on Aristotle, Aquinas, and Anscombe, but maybe also spending some time on Plato, Augustine, Descartes, Hobbes, Locke, Wittgenstein, and Ryle. In the second part of the seminar, we will look at a contemporary discussion of voluntariness in John Hyman’s book Action, Knowledge, and Will, and then at accounts of voluntariness in several parts of the law, including the definitions of consent, coercion, and negligence, as well as the definition of a voluntary act in criminal law.
